Open the courtyard toward the verified site access side.
Use a shed profile to sharpen daylight/section legibility without replacing the hall.
Keep the span axis consistent with the long bar gesture.

graph_edits.rationale: Introduce a visible public void tied to the access edge so the gym reads as approachable rather than sealed.
Align the new void to the program-frame access side to strengthen the frontage response.
Shift the hall roof family toward a clearer long-span/daylight reading while preserving the dominant bar.
Keep the roof logic aligned with the long axis of the hall for better sectional coherence.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one dominant low bar with stepped roof articulation, so it avoids the rejected 'one-view only' problem. The silhouette is not a random stair mass; the stepped profile is continuous and the volume remains legible as a single occupiable hall. Hierarchy is clear: a primary elongated mass dominates, with the stepped roof/cantilever acting as secondary sectional modulation. The main weakness is the public threshold: the blue frontage edge is answered only weakly, with no strong carved court, undercut, or entry seam, so the access response feels more sealed than welcoming. Still, for a compact training hall subtype, the massing plausibly supports the gym program: horizontal span, shallow height, and continuous section logic are all compatible, even if the roof expression is somewhat generic and the open-ground logic is underdeveloped. Parcel response is coherent; the mass sits within the boundary and aligns as a rotated bar rather than merely filling the box.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low, elongated hall-like mass with a readable ground relationship and layered roof datum.
Long-span sports volume with a strong horizontal profile and controlled public threshold.
Courtyard/entry void as a clear public-to-program transition.
Covered court logic and a legible open edge toward approach space.
